samples: This module provides an immutable last-in first-out stack: pushing or removing an item returns a new stack, peeking and popping return nothing on an empty stack, and the stack can report its size and whether it is empty. It also offers a bracket checker that says whether every round and square bracket in a piece of text is closed by the right partner in the right order, ignoring all other characters, including curly braces. Everything is pure, needing no permissions such as files or network, and it comes with examples and tests, so it is a safe, self-contained choice for simple stack needs or for validating round and square brackets, but not for checking curly braces.

This module provides a small immutable last-in first-out stack: pushing, popping and peeking return new values rather than changing the old one, and the stack can report its size and whether it is empty. It uses the stack to offer a pure checker that says whether every round `()` and square `[]` bracket in a piece of text is closed by the matching partner in the right order. Other characters are ignored, empty text counts as balanced, and the module needs no permissions, so it can be used without touching the console, files or network.

This module provides a small immutable stack: pushing or popping returns a new stack rather than changing the old one, popping or peeking an empty stack gives nothing instead of failing, and the stack can report its size and whether it is empty. On top of that it offers a pure function that checks whether the round and square brackets in a piece of text are properly paired and nested, ignoring all other characters and treating empty text as balanced. It needs no permissions such as files or network, and it ships with examples and tests, so it is a safe, self-contained choice if you need a simple stack or a bracket check, though it does not handle curly braces or other bracket types.

This module provides a simple immutable last-in first-out stack: you can create an empty one, push an item to get a new stack, pop to get the top item and the remaining stack (or nothing if it is empty), peek at the top, and ask its size or whether it is empty. It also offers a checker that says whether every round and square bracket in a piece of text is closed by the matching partner in the right order, ignoring all other characters, and returns false on the first mismatch or if any bracket is left open. It is a small, pure, self-contained utility with no side effects, documented with examples and a couple of tests, so it suits you if you need basic stack handling or a quick check of `()` and `[]` nesting, but not if you need curly braces or other bracket types.

This module provides a simple last-in first-out stack that never changes in place: pushing or popping returns a new stack, popping an empty stack gives "nothing" instead of an error, and you can peek at the top item or ask how many items it holds and whether it is empty. On top of that it offers a bracket checker that scans text and reports true only if every round and square bracket is closed by its matching partner in the correct order, ignoring all other characters, including curly braces, which are not checked. It is pure (no I/O or other capabilities needed) and comes with examples and tests, so it suits you if you need a reusable stack or a quick round/square bracket validator, but not if you need to validate curly braces.
